Learning-based transformer differential relays are rarely compared under the same data, folds and decision logic. We evaluate on simulated 300\,MVA and 40\,MVA plants with trace-grouped cross-validation (3 seeds $\times$ 5 folds, 3,302 traces) and re-implement six published methods at their own sampling rates. Natively, none reaches 93\,\% dependability and 98.8\,\% security together: the two most dependable reach 97.0\,\% and 96.5\,\% at 75.3\,\% and 82.9\,\% security. We then study a dual-path supervisory logic (an 87T vote gating a confirmed classifier output, a classifier-alone path, a high-set element) with interchangeable classifiers. With an equal search and epoch budget, six classifier instances reach 93.5--95.7\,\% dependability and 98.8--99.9\,\% security. All six are more dependable than a validation-tuned harmonic-restrained 87T (91.2\,\% / 99.1\,\%) by 2.3--4.6 points (post-hoc, trace-clustered test, Holm-adjusted), with security within $-$0.3 to +0.8 points. The deployed LSTM instance of our Simulink closed loop (93.0\,\% / 99.0\,\%) is 1.8 points more dependable than the tuned relay ($p_{\mathrm{H}}=$\,0.005), but its lead is not stable across seeds ($-$0.2 to +2.8 points). Transfer to the unseen plant depends on the classifier: zero-shot security is 99.9\,\% with Key's network but 88.4\,\% with the deployed LSTM, whose classifier-alone path caused 87 of 89 false trips. High-impedance internal faults remain a limit (dependability about 65\,\% deployed, 62\,\% tuned relay). The supervisory logic and the evaluation protocol, not the choice of classifier, are the contribution.
